title: Residue maps commute for compatible strict henselizations
statement: Let g:T→S be a scheme morphism and k,k′ separably closed fields, Ω an algebraically closed field, σ:Spec k→S, τ:Spec k′→T, ι:Spec k′→Spec k with ι≫σ=τ≫g, and ν:Spec Ω→Spec k′. Let A,B be strictly henselian local rings with separably closed residue fields, eA:Spec A≅S_(ν≫ι≫σ), eB:Spec B≅T_(ν≫τ), and residue embeddings ρA,ρB whose composites through the closed-point and structural maps equal σ and τ. There exists a local ring map φ:A→B satisfying the structural square and ρB≫Spec(ResidueField.map φ)=ι≫ρA. The map φ is chosen compatibly with the specified embeddings; this is not a claim about arbitrary independently chosen maps.

proof.text: Apply residue-image containment to get, for each x∈κA, a preimage f(x) in κB under the injective field map b to k′. Injectivity makes this preimage unique and proves the zero, one, addition and multiplication laws, giving a ring map r. The equality b∘r=a and full faithfulness of Spec give hres independently of the lifting theorem.
Apply the narrowed residue-lift theorem with the independently constructed r and hres, obtaining φ with the commuting ring residue diagram and structural square.

The composite residueB∘φ equals r∘residueA and is local, because field embeddings and residue projections are local. Hence φ is local. Surjectivity of residueA identifies r with ResidueField.map φ. Substitute this equality into the spectral residue square.

lean.statement:
theorem Etale.compatibleStrictHenselization_residue_square
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} {g : T ⟶ S}
    {k k' Ω A B : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] [Field k'] [IsSepClosed k']
    [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [HenselianLocalRing A] [HenselianLocalRing B]
    [IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)]
    [IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)]
    (σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (τ : Spec (.of k') ⟶ T)
    (ι : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (hι : ι ≫ σ = τ ≫ g)
    (ν : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec (.of k'))
    (eA : Spec (.of A) ≅ strictLocalization (ν ≫ ι ≫ σ))
    (eB : Spec (.of B) ≅ strictLocalization (ν ≫ τ))
    (ρA : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Spec (.of (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)))
    (ρB : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)))
    (hρA : ρA ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue A)) ≫
      eA.hom ≫ strictLocalizationToBase (ν ≫ ι ≫ σ) = σ)
    (hρB : ρB ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue B)) ≫
      eB.hom ≫ strictLocalizationToBase (ν ≫ τ) = τ) :
    ∃ (φ : A →+* B) (hφ : IsLocalHom φ),
      letI := hφ
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ≫ eA.hom ≫
          strictLocalizationToBase (ν ≫ ι ≫ σ) =
        eB.hom ≫ strictLocalizationToBase (ν ≫ τ) ≫ g ∧
      ρB ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map φ)) =
        ι ≫ ρA

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $g:T\to S$, the separably closed fields $k,k'$, the algebraically closed field $\Omega$, and
$\sigma,\tau,\iota,\nu$ with $\sigma\circ\iota=g\circ\tau$ be as in [compatible-strict-henselization-core-data],
with geometric points $\bar s=\sigma\iota\nu$ and $\bar t=\tau\nu$ (no integrality hypothesis is needed). Let $A$
and $B$ be henselian local rings with separably closed residue fields $\kappa_A,\kappa_B$, with isomorphisms
$e_A:\operatorname{Spec}A\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{(\bar s)}$ and $e_B:\operatorname{Spec}B\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{(\bar t)}$, and
let $\rho_A:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_A$ and $\rho_B:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_B$
satisfy
$\pi_{\bar s}\circ e_A\circ\operatorname{Spec}(A\to\kappa_A)\circ\rho_A=\sigma$ and
$\pi_{\bar t}\circ e_B\circ\operatorname{Spec}(B\to\kappa_B)\circ\rho_B=\tau$.
Then there exists a local homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$ such that
$\pi_{\bar s}\circ e_A\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=g\circ\pi_{\bar t}\circ e_B$ and the induced residue map
$\bar\varphi:\kappa_A\to\kappa_B$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{Spec}(\bar\varphi)\circ\rho_B=\rho_A\circ\iota .
$$

This asserts the existence of one compatible $\varphi$, not the compatibility of every such map.

proof.text:
The maps $\rho_A$ and $\rho_B$ correspond to field embeddings $\kappa_A\to k$ and $\kappa_B\to k'$. The image of
the composite $\kappa_A\to k\to k'$ lies in the image of $\kappa_B$, so there is a unique embedding
$r:\kappa_A\to\kappa_B$ whose composite with $\kappa_B\to k'$ is $\kappa_A\to k\to k'$; its ring laws follow from
injectivity of $\kappa_B\to k'$, and $\operatorname{Spec}(r)\circ\rho_B=\rho_A\circ\iota$ follows since
$\operatorname{Spec}$ is fully faithful. Lift $r$ through the universal property of strict henselization (Stacks
Project, Tags 04GU and 04HX) to a ring map $\varphi:A\to B$ compatible with the structure maps, which gives the
first equality. The ring residue diagram commutes and field embeddings and residue projections are local, so
$\varphi$ is local. Surjectivity of $B\to\kappa_B$ identifies $r$ with the residue map $\bar\varphi$.
